# Architecture catalog

Evidence catalog date: 2026-10-15. For changing B2 product details, use <https://www.backblaze.com/docs/cloud-storage-ai-machine-learning> as the authority.

## Stream versioned training shards from B2 to GPU workers

Package a released dataset as immutable WebDataset shards on B2, then stream them into data loaders on every worker with an optional local cache keyed by checksum.

**Use when:** Feed many GPU workers from one durable copy of a large dataset without copying it to every node first, while proving which exact dataset version each run consumed.

**Workflow:** Package a released dataset into sequential tar shards and write the shard manifest last → Pin the run to a dataset version and verify its fingerprint before training starts → Assign shards to ranks and data-loader workers → Stream shards over the S3-compatible API with ranged or sequential GETs → Cache hot shards on local NVMe keyed by SHA-256 when epochs re-read the same data → Record the dataset pin in every checkpoint and model manifest

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Scoped application keys, Multipart upload, Object versions and lifecycle rules, Event notifications, SSE-B2, Included egress to compute partners, B2 Overdrive for sustained high-throughput reads.

**Integrations:** [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — boto3 or fsspec/s3fs clients configured with the regional B2 endpoint; no PyTorch-specific B2 code is required; [WebDataset](https://github.com/webdataset/webdataset) (s3-compatible endpoint) — Shards read through fsspec URLs or a pipe command whose S3 client uses the B2 endpoint; [Ray Train, Tune, and Data](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — pyarrow.fs.S3FileSystem with endpoint_override passed as storage_filesystem or to Ray Data readers; [TensorFlow with tensorflow-io](https://github.com/tensorflow/io) (s3-compatible endpoint) — tensorflow-io S3 filesystem with the S3_ENDPOINT environment variable set to the B2 endpoint; [Hugging Face Datasets](https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/filesystems) (s3-compatible endpoint) — fsspec storage_options with client_kwargs.endpoint_url set to the B2 endpoint.

**Scale:** Multi-node GPU training reading terabytes per epoch. Standard B2 is the default. Measure per-worker throughput and GPU idle time first; consider a local cache for repeated epochs and B2 Overdrive when aggregate object-store throughput is the bottleneck.

**Security:** Give training workers read-only keys scoped to datasets/ and never the publisher key; Refuse to train when the shard manifest fingerprint differs from the pinned value; Keep keys in a secret store or Kubernetes Secret, not in container images.

**Evidence basis:** Framework source and documentation review; B2 S3 compatibility and key capability review; Moto-backed S3 application tests for streaming, fingerprint pinning, and local caching.

## Checkpoint distributed training to B2 and resume after interruption

Save sharded checkpoints to local disk, upload them to B2 with a manifest written last, resume from the newest complete checkpoint, and lock promoted checkpoints.

**Use when:** Survive node loss, preemption, and job restarts on any compute provider without losing progress or resuming from a half-written checkpoint.

**Workflow:** Save a sharded checkpoint to local staging on each rank → Upload shards in parallel with multipart transfers → Write the checkpoint manifest last as the commit marker → On restart, list checkpoints and resume from the newest one that has a manifest → Promote a selected checkpoint to an Object Lock models prefix with lineage → Prune superseded checkpoints and let lifecycle rules purge hidden versions

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Multipart upload, Scoped application keys, Server-side copy, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 and Object Lock, Event notifications, Cloud Replication for disaster recovery.

**Integrations:** [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — torch.distributed.checkpoint writes to local staging, or FsspecWriter targets s3:// paths through s3fs with the B2 endpoint; [Ray Train, Tune, and Data](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/train/user-guides/persistent-storage.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — RunConfig(storage_path=..., storage_filesystem=pyarrow.fs.S3FileSystem(endpoint_override=...)) persists Train and Tune checkpoints to B2; [PyTorch Lightning](https://lightning.ai/docs/pytorch/stable/common/checkpointing_advanced.html) (candidate, needs acceptance test) — fsspec-backed checkpoint paths with storage options for the B2 endpoint; [JAX with TensorStore](https://google.github.io/tensorstore/kvstore/s3/index.html) (candidate, needs acceptance test) — TensorStore s3 key-value store driver with its endpoint option set to the B2 endpoint; TensorStore documents that S3-compatible stores may not give the atomicity it expects, so test the checkpoint commit protocol before adopting.

**Scale:** Checkpoints from megabytes to multiple terabytes written every few minutes to hours. Upload throughput, not storage capacity, bounds checkpoint frequency. Stage locally, upload asynchronously, and parallelize per shard. Standard B2 is the default; evaluate B2 Overdrive when checkpoint upload time limits training cadence.

**Security:** Use a checkpoint writer key without deleteFiles and a separate pruning key that cannot touch models/; Promote with a key that has writeFileRetentions but not bypassGovernance; Never resume from a checkpoint whose manifest is missing or whose file checksums do not match; Treat checkpoints as sensitive when training data contains personal or licensed content.

**Evidence basis:** PyTorch and Ray checkpoint source review; B2 Object Lock, lifecycle, and key capability documentation review; Moto-backed S3 application tests for manifest-last commits, resume, promotion, and pruning.

## Track experiments and register models with a B2 artifact store

Keep tracking metadata in a database, store run artifacts and registered model files on B2, and register promoted models automatically from B2 event notifications.

**Use when:** Keep model files, evaluation artifacts, and lineage durable and shareable across teams while the tracking server stays small and stateless apart from its database.

**Workflow:** Run the tracking server with a database backend and a B2 artifact root → Log parameters, metrics, the dataset pin, and artifacts from training jobs → Register a model version from run artifacts → Promote a version by alias after evaluation → Register models written by external training jobs when their manifest-created event arrives

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Scoped application keys, Multipart upload, Event notifications, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2 and Object Lock, Presigned URLs.

**Integrations:** [MLflow](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/self-hosting/architecture/artifact-store/) (native b2 backend) — Native b2://<bucket>@s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/<path> artifact URIs; s3:// with MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL also works; [Weights & Biases](https://docs.wandb.ai/guides/artifacts/track-external-files/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — Reference artifacts on s3:// URIs with AWS_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 endpoint; [ClearML](https://clear.ml/docs/latest/docs/integrations/storage/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — output_uri on the B2 endpoint with host-specific credentials in clearml.conf; [Aim](https://aimstack.readthedocs.io/en/latest/using/artifacts.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — S3 artifacts backend with endpoint_url passed to its boto3 client; metrics and run metadata stay in Aim's local RocksDB and SQLite stores.

**Scale:** Thousands of runs per month with artifacts from kilobytes to hundreds of gigabytes. Metadata scale is bound by the tracking database, not B2. Large model files use multipart uploads from the client; proxied artifact serving moves that bandwidth onto the tracking server.

**Security:** Prefer direct client artifact access with scoped keys, or proxied serving when clients must not hold B2 credentials; Verify the X-Bz-Event-Notification-Signature header before registering anything; Make event handling idempotent because notifications are delivered at least once; Keep the tracking database and its credentials off B2.

**Evidence basis:** MLflow artifact repository source review; W&B and ClearML storage handler review; Moto-backed tests for MLflow logging, registration, and signed event handling.

## Pin dataset versions for reproducible training runs

Version training data on B2 with a data-versioning tool or immutable release prefixes, and pin every run to an exact version and fingerprint.

**Use when:** Reproduce or audit a training run months later even though the underlying dataset kept changing.

**Workflow:** Store dataset objects on B2 under a versioning tool or immutable version prefixes → Commit or tag a dataset version and record its identifier and fingerprint → Resolve the pinned version at training start and refuse mismatches → Write the pin into checkpoint, model, and tracking metadata → Retain pinned versions for as long as models trained on them are in use

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Scoped application keys, Object versions and lifecycle rules, Object Lock, Cloud Replication for disaster recovery.

**Integrations:** [lakeFS](https://docs.lakefs.io/latest/howto/deploy/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — S3 blockstore with blockstore.s3.endpoint set to the B2 endpoint and path-style addressing; [DVC](https://dvc.org/doc/user-guide/data-management/remote-storage/amazon-s3) (s3-compatible endpoint) — s3 remote with endpointurl set to the B2 endpoint; [Hugging Face Datasets](https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/filesystems) (s3-compatible endpoint) — fsspec storage_options with client_kwargs.endpoint_url set to the B2 endpoint; [Pachyderm](https://github.com/pachyderm/pachyderm/blob/master/src/internal/obj/bucket.go) (candidate, needs acceptance test) — S3 object storage through gocloud.dev blob URLs with an explicit endpoint parameter; deployment configuration and current maintenance status need confirmation on a pinned release.

**Scale:** Datasets from gigabytes to petabytes with frequent incremental updates. Versioning tools deduplicate unchanged objects, so storage grows with changed data rather than with the number of versions.

**Security:** Give training jobs read-only keys; only the versioning service or publisher writes; Protect tags or release prefixes that production models depend on from deletion; Keep versioning-tool databases and credentials off B2.

**Evidence basis:** lakeFS and DVC source review; Hugging Face Datasets filesystem documentation review; Shard manifest fingerprint pinning exercised by the PyTorch sample tests.

## Orchestrate training pipelines and retrain when new data lands

Run preprocessing, training, evaluation, and registration as pipeline steps that exchange artifacts through B2, and trigger retraining from B2 event notifications.

**Use when:** Make multi-step training workflows reproducible and restartable, and start retraining automatically when a new dataset version is published.

**Workflow:** Configure the orchestrator's artifact store on B2 → Pass step outputs between pipeline steps as B2 objects → Publish a new dataset version and write its manifest last → Receive the manifest-created event, verify it, and trigger the pipeline → Train, evaluate, and register the model with lineage to the triggering dataset version

**B2 capabilities:** S3-compatible API, Scoped application keys, Event notifications, Object versions and lifecycle rules, SSE-B2.

**Integrations:** [ZenML](https://sdkdocs.zenml.io/0.96.1/integration_code_docs/integrations-b2.html) (native b2 backend) — B2 artifact store flavor with a regional endpoint, plus the S3 flavor with a custom endpoint_url; [Kubeflow Pipelines](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/components/pipelines/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — S3-compatible object store configuration with endpoint, region, and path-style settings for the API server and launcher; [Metaflow](https://docs.metaflow.org/getting-started/infrastructure) (s3-compatible endpoint) — S3 datastore with METAFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL set to the B2 endpoint; [Flyte](https://docs.flyte.org/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — storage.type s3 with storage.connection.endpoint set to the B2 endpoint and access-key authentication; [Kedro](https://docs.kedro.org/en/stable/catalog-data/data_catalog_yaml_examples.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — Catalog credentials with client_kwargs.endpoint_url passed to s3fs; [Argo Workflows](https://argo-workflows.readthedocs.io/en/latest/configure-artifact-repository/) (s3-compatible endpoint) — S3 artifact repository with an explicit endpoint, bucket, and key secrets; [Dagster](https://docs.dagster.io/api/libraries/dagster-aws) (s3-compatible endpoint) — dagster-aws S3Resource and S3 IO managers with endpoint_url set to the B2 endpoint; [Prefect](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/main/src/integrations/prefect-aws/prefect_aws/client_parameters.py) (s3-compatible endpoint) — prefect-aws S3Bucket with AwsClientParameters(endpoint_url=...) set to the B2 endpoint; [MLRun](https://docs.mlrun.org/en/stable/store/datastore.html) (s3-compatible endpoint) — s3 datastore with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 or a DatastoreProfileS3 endpoint_url set to the B2 endpoint.

**Scale:** Tens to thousands of pipeline runs per day with intermediate artifacts of any size. Intermediate artifacts dominate object count; expire them with lifecycle rules and keep only registered models and pinned datasets long term.

**Security:** Scope each pipeline's key to its artifact prefix; Verify event signatures and deduplicate events before triggering runs; Do not give event receivers credentials that can modify datasets.

**Evidence basis:** Orchestrator artifact-store source and configuration review; B2 event notification documentation review; Signed event handling exercised by the MLflow sample tests.
